title: The Other Track
concept: Twelve days before Alaska changes governors, Governor-elect Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins asked AIDEA, a public corporation of the state, to postpone action until he takes office December 7th. The board met behind closed doors from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., took no action and resumes Friday, November 27th; its pending agenda lists ANWR, Ambler and Port MacKenzie and no data center item. The data center pieces moved earlier: AIDEA's Alaska Data Corp got a $20 million board vote, and on November 10th DNR approved giving AIDEA about 6,800 acres near Houston at no cost, land AIDEA said in July could host logistics, manufacturing and scalable data centers. Reconsideration requests are due November 30th and DNR then has 30 days, so the answer could land under the next governor, who has said he'd support a moratorium until rules exist. The test gives AIDEA's case (due diligence, the land cut from nearly 20,000 acres, a reversion clause) and the other side's (2,300+ comments, mostly opposed, a Mat-Su Borough request to reconsider) full scenes, then AIDEA's own July words: no committed tenant, power source, cooling or schedule. Drawn as a faceless switch stand at a rail fork near Houston in noon snow: a short closed AIDEA BOARD branch ending at a buffer stop, a long open DNR branch running off the frame, ties as days, and a lever caught mid-throw between RULES and a TENANT.

divergence_note: The last two films were flat July overcast over olive tundra seen from above with a faced Pi board, red GPS pins and a clipboard grid (11-24), and an apricot-plum civil twilight over lavender river ice with a scarlet ribbon, sample tubes and a cargo drone (11-23). This film is a hard low noon sun on bone haze and crusted snow, seen low and wide at a rail fork; its hero is a faceless cast-iron switch stand that acts through its lever, lamp and disc; its accent is signal amber; its shape language is divergence, a closed branch against an open one. Honest overlaps: rail appears two films after 11-23's 1925 trail (no steam, no sepia, no long single track to a vanishing point here), faceless Suits (house rig), and a tie count from above as one explainer beat.

treatment.title: The Other Track
treatment.summary: Winner C (the Explainer) with grafts from B (the Dramatist: the lever caught mid-throw between RULES and TENANT as the button, comments as mail sacks on a freight scale, the hearing at the water stop) and D (the Enthusiast: RULES ties laid ahead of an empty boxcar with its doors open that waits on the open siding). A rail junction near Houston in late-November Mat-Su snow. One track splits at a faceless switch stand: the AIDEA BOARD branch is short and closed, ending at a buffer stop with a lit window card; the Anchorage boardroom is a separate interior reached by a cut; the DNR branch is open and runs off frame into the birch. The switch stand is the protagonist and acts only through mechanism: its lever, its lamp and its target disc. Revised after Gate 0D round 1: no faced hero, no ribbon, no tag flip, no raven, no salmon, no red-family accent.
treatment.judge_reasoning: Judge reasoning: the Explainer's rail ties as days turns the thesis (the land's clock runs on DNR's reconsideration window, past the December 7th handoff) into a physical, countable picture, and the switch is the plainest image of "which track decides". The Dramatist's lever caught mid-throw between RULES and TENANT is the strongest button and the mail sacks keep residents undrawn; the Enthusiast's RULES ties laid ahead of an empty boxcar that waits lands the brand's "how could this help Alaska win" honestly. The Comedian's split frame and pie gag were funnier but carried less of the argument; the pie survives as a background gag in the boardroom. Gate 0D replaced the pitched faced survey stake with a faceless switch stand protagonist, dropped the raven and salmon, and moved the accent to signal amber. The showrunner judged the four pitches directly instead of spawning a separate scorer.

angle.thesis: Friday's AIDEA meeting isn't where Alaska's data center question gets decided. Nothing data center is on the board's agenda, the live data center clock is DNR's Houston reconsideration window that opens November 30th and could close after the handoff, and the version of this that helps Alaska win is rules before tenants.
angle.falsifiability: False if the November 27th or December 4th agenda adds a data center or Alaska Data Corp item (c13, c14, c36), or if DNR rules on the Houston reconsideration requests before December 7th (c32, c1), which would put the land question back on the outgoing clock.
supporting_facts: The pause request targets board action (c2) and the pending agenda lists ANWR, Ambler and Port MacKenzie with no data center item (c36); the board met behind closed doors and took no action (c12) and resumes November 27th (c13).

The data center pieces already moved through other doors: the $20M board vote to the AIDEA-owned Alaska Data Corp (c9, c10) and DNR's November 10th transfer of about 6,800 acres near Houston at no cost (c20), land AIDEA said in July could host scalable data centers among other uses (c22).

The land has its own clock: reconsideration due November 30th, then 30 days for DNR (c32), so an answer could land under a governor who supports a moratorium until rules exist (c11) and has said he'd completely reassess AIDEA's work (c34).
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: Two fair cases, each given a scene. AIDEA's: Ruaro says this is due diligence, not a rush (c15), with record revenue three years running (c16); Dunleavy says Alaskans elected him for a full term (c17); and the transfer was cut from nearly 20,000 acres (c21) with salmon streams and trails protected (c27) and a reversion clause (c26). The community's: more than 2,300 comments mostly opposed (c28), a unanimous Assembly (c29), the borough pointing to Point MacKenzie and its $180M rail bed (c30, c31), and a pending lawsuit (c33). And DNR says it approved a transfer, not a use (c35), while AIDEA's director called a data center there implausible in October (c38).
angle.valence: curious and constructive. The capital pitch behind AI infrastructure is real (c37, the pitch not a project) and Alaska has a funded vehicle (c10). Rules first loses nothing that exists today, because AIDEA itself listed no tenant, power source, cooling or schedule (c24). Neither side is a villain; the film ends on a question of order.
angle.who_it_serves: Mat-Su residents and the borough, who have a live way to be heard by November 30th (c30, c32); legislators and the incoming team watching the handoff; and anyone who wants Alaska to land AI infrastructure capital (c37) on a site that won't be fought in court (c33).
angle.second_movement: DNR says its decision covers the transfer, not the use (c35), and the borough isn't refusing industry, it names other sites (c30, c31). So even the land clock doesn't decide what gets built. What decides it is whether rules arrive before a tenant does (c11, c24).

runner_up_angles.angle: The lame-duck rush is a power grab
runner_up_angles.lost_because: claims a motive the record doesn't show: closed session, no action (c12), a request not an order (c2), Ruaro rejects rushing (c15)

runner_up_angles.angle: A pause throws away Alaska's head start in the AI data center race
runner_up_angles.lost_because: no data center vote is pending (c36), no tenant, power or schedule (c24), no project identified (c25); the head start is a pitch (c37)

runner_up_angles.angle: Nothing data center is moving, so the fight is theatre
runner_up_angles.lost_because: the $20M vote is done (c10), the land moved November 10th (c20), the reconsideration clock runs past the handoff (c32), 2,300+ comments (c28)

angle.cross_challenge: Three analysts (structural, enthusiast, dramatist) each red-teamed two of the three rivals above; all three converged on the separate-clock reading. The enthusiast's 'rules first loses nothing that exists today' is grafted as the button; the dramatist's community-as-civic-process is the Act 3 scene; the structural reading's 'transfer, not use' is the second movement.
angle.absence_checks: No data center item: read the November 24th continued agenda in full (executive session topics, Resolutions G26-05, G26-07, G26-01, directors comment). The governor-elect's statement doesn't mention data centers (Must Read Alaska quotes it at length). Neither ADN November 11th nor the pause coverage mentions AI; the only AI line is the Plural CEO in the InvestNorth launch release.
angle.distinct_from_recent: 10-20 asked whether the land should pass before anyone can say what will be built (preliminary decision); 11-13 asked rules first or money first for tokenized stakes; this film is about which clock decides, after the transfer and the pause request.

open_loop.what: What is down the other track? Planted as the lamp flares and the stand's long shadow stretches down the open DNR branch past a milepost reading DNR, STATE LAND NEAR HOUSTON, running off the frame; carried as the land's clock is set on that branch; paid when an empty boxcar on that branch rolls its doors open on nothing inside: no committed tenant, power source, cooling or schedule.

open_loop_2.what: Does the land decide what gets built? Planted as three use cards spring up on the parcel, COULD HOST, and the points slide toward a siding that curves out of sight; paid when a DNR stamp lands on the ACRES car: THE TRANSFER, NOT THE USE.
